experiment: Silhouette-based page classification for scanned årsregnskap
status: Informative but insufficient for production use
approach: Render pages at low DPI (36-72), extract spatial features from grayscale thumbnails and diagnostic bands, classify by template matching

methods_tested.name: 48x48 thumbnail features (quadrant means, row/col variance, edge density)
methods_tested.notes: Features separate populations but overlap at decision boundaries

methods_tested.name: Boundary detection via consecutive BRREG-like signature
methods_tested.failure_mode: Generell_info page has different footer than other BRREG pages; sparse BRREG continuation pages look like company signatur pages

methods_tested.name: Template divergence from page 1
methods_tested.failure_mode: Silvercoin company pages visually similar to BRREG template; distance threshold cannot separate

methods_tested.name: 16-bin band signature template matching (72 DPI)
methods_tested.boundary_accuracy: 0/4 (page 1 always misclassified; Silvercoin company section uses BRREG-like template)
methods_tested.failure_mode: Generell_info has footer='Utskriftsdato' not 'Side X av Y' — different bottom band. Silvercoin company pages have top_d=0.4, bot_d=3.4 — identical to BRREG

key_findings: All 5 test PDFs are scanned images (1728x2312 PNG/page, zero text layer) — text-based features impossible
BRREG template IS visually distinctive: top_band ~254 (white header), specific bottom-left dark band (Brønnøysundregistrene text)
Generell_info (page 1) is always an outlier — different footer pattern than other BRREG pages
CRITICAL: Some companies (Silvercoin) use templates visually indistinguishable from BRREG at pixel level — band signatures match within threshold. This is a hard ceiling for pixel-only approaches.
Company signatur pages (mostly white with a few lines of text) look identical to sparse BRREG continuation pages in pixel features
Best achievable source accuracy with pixels alone: ~75-80%. Not sufficient for production where misclassifying source causes hallucinated company values.

comparison_with_gemini.gemini_classify_pdf_accuracy: 100% on all 4 labeled entities (per manifest experiment)
comparison_with_gemini.conclusion: Gemini reads the actual text ('Brønnøysundregistrene', 'Side X av Y') which is unambiguous. Pixel silhouettes capture visual layout but cannot distinguish templates that LOOK similar but have different TEXT content. The 25% error rate is concentrated in exactly the cases that matter most: generell_info pages and company sections with BRREG-like formatting.

generalizing_to_sections.feasibility: Low for fine-grained type classification, moderate for coarse binary (has_table vs narrative)
generalizing_to_sections.table_detection: 73% accuracy from row_var + col_var features — dense number tables have distinctively high column variance
generalizing_to_sections.type_classification: 52% — too many visual overlaps between resultatregnskap/balanse/noter, all of which are 'table with numbers'
generalizing_to_sections.recommendation: Pixel features could pre-filter pages into has_table/no_table before Gemini extraction, potentially allowing skipping Gemini for clearly narrative pages. But the cost saving ($0.0001 per skipped page) does not justify the false negative risk.

verdict: The silhouette approach confirms that BRREG pages have a distinctive visual signature (consistent header/footer bands, specific text density patterns). However, pixel features hit a hard ceiling at ~75% because some company templates are visually identical to BRREG. For a pipeline where source misclassification causes Gemini to hallucinate company financial values (the most dangerous error type identified in the manifest experiment), 75% is unacceptable. Gemini classify_pdf at $0.0003 remains the production classifier.
